newsitem.title: UK: Stocks fall in Europe, Asia.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall in Europe, Asia.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Friday.

LONDON - British shares gave back all of Thursday's gains as investors worried that Wall Street could be on the verge of a major correction. The FTSE 100 ended 52.7 points down at 4,218.8. Over the week the FTSE gained 11.1 points.

FRANKFURT - German stocks ended bourse trade lower in sympathy with Wall Street's overnight tumble, but dealers said this was not the large-scale correction many have been waiting for. The DAX-30 index ended at 2,998.24 points, down 35.22 points for a small drop of 3.13 on the week. In post-bourse trade the index fell 54.65 to 2,982.63.

PARIS - French shares closed 1.26 percent lower on profit-taking after an overnight fall on Wall Street signalled to investors that a boisterous start to the year's bull run could have ended. French shares, retracing from a record close on Thursday, did not extend their losses by much in the afternoon when Wall Street made fresh declines.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 30.91 points at 2,430.34. This week the CAC-40 gained 5.24 points.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended 1 percent lower on the back of a Wall Street slump on Thursday but the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) managed to close above 4,100 points after temporarily falling below that level. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 20.54 points to 2,639.55 but up 60.29 on the week.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks finished sharply lower, haunted by worries over the financial health of the banking sector and intermittent bouts of futures-linked selling, stemming from a lack of confidence in the future of the economy. The 225-share Nikkei average finished trade down 220.10 points at 17,689.36 a fall of 400.60 on the week.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks slid to a sharply lower close after a drop on Wall Street overnight left investors jittery going into the weekend. The Hang Seng Index dropped 230.78 points to 13,379.55 down 476.85 from last weeks close.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market closed lower after Wall Street tumbled with only an heroic performance from National Australia Bank, buoyed by Thursday's first quarter profit, preventing further losses. The All Ordinaries index fell 11.5 points to 2,423.0 and down 12.5 from last Friday.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares regained some of their earlier losses just before the close of trade on short-covering after hitting day lows in the afternoon in the wake of weaker world markets.

The industrial index recovered from 70 points down in afternoon trade to close 40.3 points off at 8,042.8, down 137.6 on the week. The overall index lost 33.3 points to 6,684.6, a loss of 98.3 since last Friday, and the gold index was up 17.2 points to 1,370.4 points, but down 55.8 form last week's close.
